newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian edible oil prices fall on adequate supplies.
newsitem.headline: Indian edible oil prices fall on adequate supplies.

text.p: Indian edible oil prices eased during the week on sustained imports and good domestic arrivals but the progress of the monsoon would determine prices in June, traders said on Wednesday.
"The market is absolutely weak because of domestic arrivals and imports," Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
Shah said plenty of edible oil was available but buying activity was at a virtual standstill.
Traders said prices of most edible oils were falling by 100-200 rupees per tonne every day.

They said palm olein was quoted at about 27,400 rupees per tonne in the local markets, against 29,500 rupees about 20 days ago. Groundnut oil was quoted at 35,500-36,000 rupees per tonne compared with 37,000 rupees in the past fortnight.
Shah said about 7,000 to 10,000 tonnes of imported palm olein, sunflower oil, cotton and soybean oils were arriving every week at the Bombay port alone.
Traders estimated imports of about 130,000 tonnes of edible oil in June. In May, 100,000 tonnes had already arrived.
"After a fortnight, the prices will be determined by the behaviour of the monsoon," Shah said.
The Meteorological Department said on Sunday that India's annual monsoon, crucial to agriculture, is likely to yield a normal amount of rainfall for the 10th successive year in 1997.
The southwest monsoon rains usually strike the southwestern coast around June 1 and cover the entire country before tapering off in September.

Analysts said edible oil prices would be steady until July. The domestic demand would start picking up from August with the start of the festival season, after low demand in the summer months of May to July, they said. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
